# Test fixtures

Everything here is generated by `scripts/make_fixtures.py` except the face photo. Run `just fixtures` on macOS (it needs `say` and ffmpeg) to regenerate it all from scratch. Two runs give identical decoded streams and identical ground truth; only container and encoder metadata may differ.

## Files

| Path | Committed | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `media/en_talking.mov` | no | English talking clip, voice Samantha (en_US), with a presenter video at 1080×1920 that shows the face photo |
| `media/it_talking.mov` | no | Italian talking clip, voice Alice (it_IT), same video |
| `media/prova clip è.mov` | no | A byte copy of `en_talking.mov`, for paths with spaces and accents. Its ground truth is `en_talking.json`. |
| `media/broll.mp4` | no | 6 s of ffmpeg `testsrc2` at 1920×1080, 30 fps, with quiet seeded pink noise and no speech |
| `media/image.png` | no | ffmpeg `mandelbrot` frame, 1600×1200 |
| `tiny.mp4` | yes | 2 s of `testsrc2` at 360×640 with a 440 Hz `sine`, for fast tests (about 110 KB) |
| `ground_truth/en_talking.json`, `ground_truth/it_talking.json` | yes | What the script inserted into each talking clip |
| `faces/neil_armstrong_960.jpg` | yes | Public-domain face photo for face-detection tests |

`media/` is gitignored. Tests that need it are marked `slow` and `mac`.

## Talking clips

Each line is spoken by `say` on its own, trimmed to its audible part, and joined with silences of exact length written as zero samples. The ground truth comes from those sample counts, not from measuring the result.

Each clip has five utterances and ends in 3 s of silence: a greeting, a line with a hard filler (`um` or `ehm`) between two 300 ms pauses, an abandoned first attempt, its complete retake, and a sign-off. The audio is 48 kHz mono AAC.

The video is a "presenter": the face photo, cropped to 500 px around the face and shown 720 px wide, drifts over a flat box, then holds still for the 3 s silent tail, so analyze finds a face in every sampled frame and reports the tail as static. It is encoded at 30 fps without B-frames, then remuxed with the `setts` bitstream filter so every third frame arrives 10 ms late. Frame durations alternate 43, 23 and 33 ms: `avg_frame_rate` is `30/1` but `r_frame_rate` reads `300/1`, so read the frame rate from `avg_frame_rate`.

## Ground truth format

Times are integer milliseconds from the start of the clip. The example is abridged from `en_talking.json`.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "clip": "en_talking.mov",
  "language": "en",
  "voice": "Samantha",
  "duration_ms": 20833,
  "video": {"width": 1080, "height": 1920, "fps": 30, "vfr": true},
  "utterances": [{"text": "Hi, welcome back to the channel.", "start_ms": 800, "end_ms": 2758, "complete": true}],
  "fillers": [{"text": "um", "kind": "hard", "start_ms": 5049, "end_ms": 5368}],
  "silences": [{"start_ms": 0, "end_ms": 800, "context": "head"}],
  "retake": {"abandoned": 2, "winner": 3}
}
```

- `utterances` are in order. A filler and its two pauses lie inside the utterance that contains them, and the filler is part of its `text`.
- `silences` lists every inserted silence. `context` is `head`, `between_utterances`, `around_filler` or `tail`. The tail is padded up to a whole video frame.
- `retake` holds indices into `utterances`: the abandoned attempt (`complete: false`) and the complete retake that should win the retake cluster.
